purpose: Three isolated global visual-style block candidates for the D1/D2/D3 Japanese collectible-anime house-style calibration, following the A/B/C round (which removed the stock-photo look but did not land the intended Japanese commercial-anime/collectible-card energy). Each block REPLACES only global_style_v1.json's top-level `prompt` field for the purposes of this test; global_text_policy, global_screen_policy, and global_negatives are reused unchanged from production so semantic/content-safety behavior is held constant across D1/D2/D3.

D1.label: Balanced Japanese Collectible Lifestyle (50/50)
D1.description: ~50% Japanese collectible-card/commercial-anime energy + 50% grounded real-world lifestyle storytelling.
D1.prompt:
STYLE BALANCE D1:

Use an approximately equal balance between Japanese collectible-card anime illustration and contemporary real-world lifestyle storytelling.

The hobby activity and believable social environment are equally important to the collectible visual energy.

Keep the anime influence clearly visible through:
- linework
- cel shading
- expressive faces
- clean silhouettes
- bright color
- lively gesture
- polished illustrated lighting

But keep people, objects, activities and environments relatively grounded.

Do not exaggerate expressions or poses too far.

Do not turn everyday activities into fantasy scenes.

The intended result is:
“a beautiful real-world lifestyle moment illustrated by a top Japanese commercial anime artist and designed to feel collectible.”

Maintain warmth and natural social interaction.

This version should be the most grounded of D1/D2/D3 while still being unmistakably Japanese-anime illustrated.

Create a premium, original Japanese-inspired collectible hobby illustration for Zync.

This must be clearly illustrated artwork, not photography.

The visual language should feel like polished contemporary Japanese commercial anime illustration and premium collectible-card artwork applied to real-world hobbies.

The image should feel:
- joyful
- colorful
- charming
- energetic
- optimistic
- youthful but not childish
- polished
- iconic
- emotionally inviting
- highly collectible

The hobby subject or central human interaction must feel like the HERO of the illustration.

Do not depict merely an ordinary documentary moment.

Instead depict a memorable “best moment” of doing, discovering, sharing, mastering, enjoying, or becoming excited by the hobby.

Use:
- clean, confident Japanese anime-style linework
- polished cel shading
- soft painted gradients
- crisp subject separation
- expressive faces
- bright, clear eyes
- slightly stylized facial proportions
- stylized but believable anatomy
- elegant simplified forms
- lively natural gestures
- dynamic but readable poses
- strong silhouettes
- intentional hero framing
- colorful, harmonious palettes
- saturated but controlled color
- attractive complementary color relationships
- luminous highlights
- colorful rim-light accents where appropriate
- subtle sparkle or glint accents
- soft environmental particles only when they enhance mood
- expressive environment design
- charming visual details
- graphic shape language
- strong foreground/midground/background separation

The environment must remain believable and relevant to the real-world hobby, but should be interpreted as a beautifully designed anime environment rather than a real photograph.

Simplify reality.

Do not render every tiny real-world detail.

Use selective visual detail and stylization so the image feels drawn and intentionally designed.

The image should have a clear visual hierarchy:
1. hero subject / hero interaction
2. hobby-defining objects or action
3. supporting environment
4. small delightful details

Use subtle heightened visual energy to make the scene collectible.

This may include:
- gentle glowing edge light
- sparkling highlights
- soft color accents
- subtle atmospheric movement
- floating dust/pollen/light flecks
- stylized steam
- wind in clothing/hair
- motion accents
- attractive graphic color shapes

But these effects must NOT transform the hobby into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself calls for fantasy.

The result must remain a real-world hobby scene.

Default emotional direction:

joyful,
optimistic,
curious,
friendly,
energetic,
aspirational,
inviting,
playful,
emotionally alive.

Prefer moments of:
- discovery
- connection
- excitement
- mastery
- friendship
- satisfaction
- surprise
- delight
- fascination

Even serious or intellectual hobbies must feel visually inviting.

For example:

Philosophy should NOT default to:
- gloomy scholars
- sombre brown libraries
- depressing introspection
- dark academic solemnity

Instead it may show:
- animated discussion
- curiosity
- a breakthrough moment
- friends debating ideas
- bright books/notebooks/visual cues
- intellectual excitement

“Knowledge is exciting,” not “knowledge is heavy.”

Legal thriller may be tense, but should still feel visually compelling, stylish and collectible rather than grim or bleak.

Do NOT render:

- real photography
- stock photography
- lifestyle advertising photography
- DSLR realism
- documentary realism
- photojournalism
- cinematic live-action film stills
- photographic skin pores
- photographic depth of field
- real-camera bokeh
- lens artifacts
- camera-real exposure behavior
- photobashing
- Western oil-paint concept art
- gritty Western fantasy concept art
- muted brown editorial palettes
- beige corporate lifestyle advertising
- flat corporate vector illustration
- generic Silicon Valley illustration style
- generic Western magazine editorial art
- New Yorker-style restrained editorial illustration
- dark prestige-TV realism
- gloomy academic illustration
- generic fantasy splash-art chaos
- excessive magic
- battle effects unrelated to the hobby
- glowing supernatural aura
- fantasy weapons or magical relics unless the hobby requires them
- chibi proportions
- preschool cartoon proportions
- hypersexualized anime proportions
- exaggerated fan-service posing
- official TCG UI
- card frames
- white card margins
- decorative collectible-card borders
- HP bars
- stats panels
- attack boxes
- elemental/type icons
- rarity stars
- franchise logos
- recognizable copyrighted characters

IMPORTANT:

The artwork itself must be full-bleed, edge-to-edge illustration.

Do NOT draw a physical card around the artwork.

No border.
No mat.
No card shell.
No rounded white frame.
No decorative frame.
No printed-paper edge.

The application will handle the actual card UI later.

Do not imitate any existing entertainment or collectible-card franchise directly.

Do not reproduce:
- recognizable franchise characters
- recognizable franchise creatures
- recognizable franchise visual motifs
- logos
- official trading-card layouts
- card borders
- HP bars
- attack boxes
- type/element icons
- rarity badges
- stats
- title bars
- game UI

The result should feel like a distinct Zync house style:

bright,
joyful,
Japanese-inspired,
commercial-anime polished,
human-centered,
modern,
collectible,
energetic,
friendly,
premium,
and clearly illustrated.

Hard visual constraints:

The image must immediately read as Japanese-inspired commercial anime illustration.

Do not render a photograph.
Do not render a stock lifestyle image.
Do not render a Western editorial illustration.
Do not render gritty Western concept art.
Do not render muted serious book-cover art.
Do not render corporate flat-vector art.

Faces, clothing, objects, backgrounds, lighting and textures must all visibly belong to the same polished anime illustration language.

The image should feel joyful and collectible before it feels realistic.

D2.label: Joyful Japanese Collectible (60/40)
D2.description: ~60% Japanese collectible-card/commercial-anime energy + 40% grounded real-world lifestyle storytelling.
D2.prompt:
STYLE BALANCE D2:

Push the image clearly toward premium Japanese collectible-card / commercial anime illustration.

Target approximately:
60% Japanese collectible anime energy
40% grounded real-world lifestyle storytelling.

The anime/card-art component should visibly dominate the visual language.

Increase:
- expressive facial animation
- confident clean linework
- cel-shaded form definition
- bright controlled saturation
- attractive color contrast
- stronger hero framing
- more dynamic pose/gesture
- clearer silhouette
- luminous edge highlights
- tasteful sparkle/glint accents
- environmental movement
- emotional immediacy
- charming visual detail
- “special moment” energy

The scene should feel like a highly desirable collectible illustration rather than simply an illustrated lifestyle scene.

Make the main subject feel iconic.

Characters should feel charismatic and memorable.

Their reactions should be more expressive than ordinary reality while still believable.

Use playful perspective and slightly heightened composition when useful.

The environment remains a real place and the hobby remains completely real-world.

Do NOT introduce fantasy lore, magical powers or battle imagery.

The heightened quality should come from:
- expression
- color
- lighting
- composition
- movement
- visual charm

not supernatural content.

For social hobbies:
make relationships and reactions vivid and joyful.

For food:
make the food visually delicious with appealing anime-style gloss, steam, color and highlights.

For fashion:
give the subject confident hero-character presence and stronger outfit silhouette.

For intellectual topics:
show curiosity, energetic debate, discovery or insight rather than solemn academic seriousness.

For serious entertainment genres:
retain appropriate tension, but render it with stylized Japanese visual drama rather than Western live-action darkness.

Grounded realism remains present, but it is clearly subordinate to the joyful Japanese collectible illustration language.

This version should feel closest to:
“real human hobbies elevated into premium Japanese collectible character-and-world illustrations.”

D3.label: Strong Japanese Collectible Anime (70/30)
D3.description: ~70% Japanese collectible-card/commercial-anime energy + 30% grounded lifestyle realism.
D3.prompt:
STYLE BALANCE D3:

Push strongly toward premium Japanese commercial anime and collectible-card illustration.

Target approximately:
70% Japanese collectible anime energy
30% grounded lifestyle realism.

The final image must still depict the correct real-world hobby, but the visual language should be unmistakably stylized, colorful, energetic and collectible.

Strongly emphasize:
- crisp anime line art
- elegant cel shading
- bold yet tasteful color
- expressive faces
- larger emotional reactions
- strong character appeal
- dynamic gestures
- heroic subject positioning
- dramatic but clean perspective
- attractive rim lighting
- graphic lighting shapes
- colorful atmospheric accents
- sparkling highlights
- stylized motion
- idealized “best moment” storytelling
- polished commercial-anime finish

The central character or interaction should feel like the protagonist of their own hobby world.

The scene may be visually heightened and idealized.

It should feel exciting enough that a user would want to collect the illustration even if they did not already practice the hobby.

However:

Do NOT make the characters chibi.
Do NOT make them children unless the hobby/context explicitly calls for children.
Do NOT create fantasy creatures.
Do NOT create magical powers.
Do NOT create battle scenes.
Do NOT turn real hobby equipment into fantasy weapons.
Do NOT lose hobby recognition.

Real-world semantics remain mandatory.

The higher anime percentage applies only to:
- rendering
- expression
- color
- composition
- visual energy
- charm
- illustration language

not to changing the content into fantasy.

For serious subjects, retain contextual seriousness but make the artwork attractive, dynamic and emotionally engaging rather than gloomy.

This version should feel like:
“a premium Japanese collectible anime illustration whose subject happens to be a real-world hobby.”
